messages.subject: Re: Launching JGR consumes %99 of CPU
messages.body_plain:
On Dec 4, 2006, at 7:15 AM, Ilhami Visne wrote:

> As i wrote in subject, launching JGR consumes %99 of cpu and it  
> takes  ~35 seconds untill it shows up. is it normal or is something  
> wrong by me?
>
> my laptop's cpu is centrino 1.86 and i have 2 GB Ram. i don't think  
> that my laptop is slow for an application like JGR or at least just  
> for starting.
>

All JGR does is to start JVM and then R subsequently. Depending on  
the machine this will take some time, but even for my old desktop  
test machine it is only a few seconds.

When you start JVM (and R) the first time it is usually a very disk- 
intensive task and laptops tend to have very slow disks, so it may  
take longer than on other machines. Also depending on your drivers  
IDE I/O tends to be hogging CPU on Windows, so I could well imagine  
this being accompanied with 100% CPU usage.

However, starting JGR the second time should be much faster. If it's  
not, then there is some other issue.

Also some versions of JGR start the help system right away (i.e. you  
see the R console but it is still not responsive). This could be  
disabled - so the question in what state  is JGR when you experience  
'unexpected' delays.

Cheers,
Simon

messages.subject: some configuration issues / future of jgr
messages.subject_clean: some configuration issues / future of jgr
messages.body_plain:
Hallo everybody!

I am using JGR 1.4-7 on Mac OS X 10.3.9.



1. Is there a way to configure JGR to *fully* restore a previously saved 
workspace, including option settings and the .First function?

I wanted to configure some (options and library) settings when R starts 
up so I defined a '.First' function as suggested by the R manual.

Everything works fine when using R from the command line:
- define '.First'
- save workspace on exit
- start R: '.First()' is there and executed
   (libraries loaded, options set).

When starting JGR, though, neither has '.First' been run nor does it 
appear in the objects listing, 'ls(all=T)' -- i.e. it doesn't exist.

Putting a '.First' or just the commands into a '.RProfile' does not help 
either.



2. Is there a way to configure the package installer so that it does use 
the options settings rather than defaulting to "binary"?

Since I am still running Mac OS 10.3, I need an 
'options(pkgType="source")' (hence my trouble explained in no. 1).

There is the nice menu "Package Installer". Now this calls 
'installPackages()' from 'jgr.supplements' using the default 
'type=binary' -- unlike 'install.packages()' from 'base' which uses, 
correctly IMHO, 'type=options("pkgType")'. There is, BTW, also a naming 
mismatch, since 'install.packages()' has types "source", "mac.binary" 
and "win.binary", whereas 'installPackages()' has "source" and "binary" 
(i.e generic "binary" instead of ).

Of course, this is not a big issue since 'installPackages()' or rather 
'install.packages()' can be called from the JGR console -- it just would 
be nice to be able to configure the menu too.

(Point 1. and 2. may be summarized thus: JGR doesn't properly respect 
user settings and definitions.)



3. General question: What are the future plans for JGR development?

There are, obviously, some important parts missing, esp. the ability to 
edit/fix objects through the object browser.

I am just asking because I see that JGR is developed by a university's 
research institute, but two of the main developers have left that 
institute (probably doing exciting stuff elsewhere!) and there is no 
indication as to where JGR is heading in what time frame.



Cheers and Thanks!
-- 
Ulf Martin
ulfmartin at web.de

It seems as if you un-installed R after installing, because the  
crucial entry SOFTWARE\\R-core\\R\InstallPath is missing. You have  
only the left-overs from versioned installs.

You must always install new R version as the last step. If you  
uninstall any R version after that, it will delete the above entry,  
regardless of the fact that another R version is still installed.  
Please re-install R to fix that (or create the entry manually if you  
wish).

Cheers,
Simon

That is in fact a valid question. As Markus was saying, we'll  
definitely make sure that JGR is available for upcoming R versions. I  
am maintaining all the "glue" code and I plan to do so in the future.

As of future development, it would be really nice if someone would  
step up to add new features to JGR. The source code is publicly  
available (see rforge.net) and adding new features is not very hard  
due to the modular design of JGR. I think it would be a nice student  
project, especially since everything is publicly available on CRAN.  
Many aspects of JGR could be improved even without touching the  
original source code, just leveraging JRI/rJava and adding new  
classes. If anyone is interested in that sort of thing, I'm willing  
to help with the details.

Cheers,
Simon

messages.subject: Re: JRI limitation on RMainLoopCallbacks.rReadConsole
messages.body_plain:
Brian,

On Dec 7, 2006, at 6:02 PM, Brian Fjeldstad wrote:

> It seems that any String returned from an implementation of  
> RMainLoopCallbacks.rReadConsole is truncated at or around 1024  
> characters.
>

Yes, that is a property of R which calls R_ReadConsole with a pre- 
defined buffer whose length is 1024 bytes.

I'm not quite sure how to handle this properly. Probably the most  
clean way is to add int length to the parameters of the rReadConsole  
callback, so that the application knows what the limit is. Right now  
the string is silently truncated to fit the length supported by R. In  
theory the internal implementation in of JRI could split the returned  
string to chunks according to the called length, but that it not  
quite correct, because it doesn't have the ability to display prompt  
etc. and thus the numer of callback will be different from what R  
receives. Any suggestions are welcome...

Cheers,
Simon

messages.subject: Re: Build a matrix using JRI
messages.body_plain:
François,

On Dec 22, 2006, at 5:03 AM, Francois EHRENMANN wrote:

> I'm a new user of R and JRI for a project (debian + eclipse + Java  
> + JRI).
>
> I need to build a matrix from datas and i proceed like this :
>
> First step :  create the  matrix (Rengine re)
> re.idleEval("A <- mat.or.vec(10,40)",true);
>
> Second Step : feed the structure
> re.idleEval("A[1,1] <- 39",true);
> re.idleEval("A[1,2] <- 10",true);
> re.idleEval("A[1,3] <- 5",true);
> ...
> re.idleEval("A[10,40] <- 16",true);
>

Using "idle"Eval" is not a good idea - it doesn't guarantee that the  
code gets executed - it is only meant for periodic evaluations where  
you don't mind if it is not evaluated because R is busy.

Also the above is very inefficient. You can use something like this:

double a[10*40] = {39, 10, 5, ..., 16};

re.assign("A", a);
re.eval("A<-matrix(A, 10, 40, TRUE)");

> I want finaly to obtain the matrix result, passing these datas to R :
> REXP x = re.idleEval("A", true);
> and i make this command to see results :
> Supervisor.trace(this, x.toString());
>
> and i have as output :
>
> [REAL* (39.0, 10.0, 5.0, 24.0, 30.0, 5.0, 9.0, 16.0, 0.0, 0.0, 4.0,  
> 4.0, 2.0, 4.0, 4.0, 4.0, 2.0, 2.0, 0.0, 0.0, 3.0, 3.0, 2.0, 1.0,  
> 3.0, 3.0, 2.0, 3.0, 0.0, 0.0, 2.0, 2.0, 4.0, 4.0, 4.0, 4.0, 2.0,  
> 1.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0, 1.0, 2.0, 1.0, 3.0, 3.0, 2.0, 2.0, 0.0, 0.0,  
> 4.0, 4.0, 1.0, 1.0, 2.0, 2.0, 1.0, 1.0, 0.0, 0.0, 2.0, 2.0, 0.0,  
> 2.0, 2.0, 8.0, 3.0, 1.0, 0.0, 0.0, 2.0, 2.0, 0.0, 1.0, 2.0, 0.0,  
> 2.0, 3.0, 0.0, 0.0, 4.0, 4.0, 0.0, 2.0, 2.0, 0.0, 1.0, 2.0, 0.0,  
> 0.0, 3.0, 3.0, 0.0, 2.0, 2.0, 0.0, 3.0, 4.0, 0.0, 0.0, ... (300  
> more values follow))]
>

You are looking the the result on the Java side and you (correctly)  
get a real vector of the length 400. You could get the original  
contents with
double d[] = x.asDoubleArray();

> Passing my datas to R (using R in a console), i obtain this output  
> that i want to have using java and JRI but it doesn't work :
>

Well, you didn't ask for it. If you want the textual output, you can  
either use the console:

re.eval("print(A)")

or if you need the string result programmatically, you can use  
something like this:

String text = re.eval("paste(capture.output(print(A)),collapse='\ 
\n')").asString();

Cheers,

messages.subject: Re: RServe session management
messages.body_plain:
Tamir,

On Dec 22, 2006, at 8:32 AM, Ido M. Tamir wrote:

> I have learned, that RServe/JRClient now supports detaching and  
> reattaching to
> a session.
>
> A) is it possible to attach to an RSession from a different VM?

Yes

> or to rephrase, do the sessions have some form of ID that can be  
> read such
> that attaching from a different program would be possible somehow?

Yes - see the RSession object - you can serialize it and use in a  
different JVM.

> Is it possible to get a list of the current sessions?
>

No, there is not real session management. The serving processes are  
independent once connected, so the main Rserve process doesn't know  
(or care) which sessions are active.

>

> B) How are sessions managed in respect to processing resources? Are  
> concurrent requests within different session queued?
>

"different" session? No - all sessions are completely independent and  
work in parallel. If you have a SMP machine, they will be using one  
CPU each (if available).

> C) Why is it Rconnection and Rtalk (lower case) but RObject, RModel..
> (upper case?)
>

Rxxx classes are older than RXxx classes.


> D) I just installed Rserve on fc5 x86_64 and I got:
> "Rserve binary was installed in libs because multi-arch support is  
> enabled."
>> ../inst/Rserve-bin.txt;
> so I had to manually create a symbolic link to enable R CMD Rserve
> ln -s /usr/lib64/R/library/Rserve/Rserve /usr/lib64/R/bin/Rserve
>

Yes, given that you appear to have R with multiple architectures  
installed, it doesn't make sense to put Rserve in $R_HOME/bin  
automatically, because it would overwrite any other architecture you  
had there before. If you use Rserve() it will always start the  
correct binary even in multi-arch setup.

Cheers,
Simon
